question: A normal chest radiograph in a patient with symptoms of COPD reliably excludes the diagnosis and means spirometry is not required.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. The chest radiograph is normal in up to 50% of patients with mild COPD. It is used to exclude differentials (pneumonia, pneumothorax, malignancy), not to confirm or refute COPD. Spirometry remains the diagnostic gold standard.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Chest X-ray is insensitive for COPD, particularly in mild-to-moderate disease. Spirometry (FEV1/FVC < 0.70 post-bronchodilator) is the diagnostic reference standard; a normal CXR does not exclude COPD.
